details:
Q1: How should a same-repo run be handled when the heal issue has no head SHA and no PR or branch to check it against? This is common for heal issues created from an escalation label on an issue.
Choices:
A) Skip it, the same way cross-repo runs are skipped today. Record the reason under `Skipped` in `INDEX.md` (`run_no_verified_context`). Same-repo runs are kept only when their head SHA matches and their branch, linked PR, or `[pr:N]` run name matches too. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Same as A, plus one extra rule for issue escalations: also accept a run when the API reports its `head_branch` as `ai/issue-<N>`, where N is the escalated issue's number. This keeps evidence for pipeline issues in this repo, and links from outside commenters to other runs are still rejected.
C) Keep accepting same-repo runs that have no context, but only when their workflow file is one of the pipeline workflows (clarify, plan, implement, review, orchestrate, validate, release). **Note:** this still accepts an unrelated run of those workflows, so it only partly closes the finding.
Q2: Should this PR also change the reporter (`build_issue_payload` / `extract_run_refs` in `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`) so it stops copying run links from untrusted comments?
Choices:
A) No. Fix only the collector. It is where the GH_PAT reads happen, so binding runs there is enough. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Yes, as an extra layer. Take run links only from the issue body and from comments by `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` or the bot account. Also keep the collector fix.
